requirements.summary: The installed rule targets the exact log and parses as a one-day rotation policy. The enabled, active daily logrotate timer had its next execution scheduled, a forced run successfully rotated the target, and the rule and timer persisted after restart.

The configured policy specifies seven compressed rotations. A controlled exercise produced exactly app.log.1.gz through app.log.7.gz, all passed gzip validation, no eighth archive existed, and the count and checksums remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote afterward. The active log retained its inode, the pre-rotation marker appeared in the compressed archive, and the post-rotation marker appeared in the active log. Post-restart writing also succeeded.

overall_summary: All three public task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot identity appeared, and system, timer, configuration, archive, data, and write health recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The evidence window did not include a naturally triggered midnight rotation; daily cadence is demonstrated by the parsed one-day rule, active daily timer, and forced functional rotation.
No inventory application process was present during discovery; write continuity was therefore tested with an equivalent descriptor held open across rotation.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the rule was required; forced rotations and marker appends were bounded functional and retention verification; the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol; and the temporary checksum manifest was removed. The two nonzero commands were read-only polls interrupted by the reboot. Final observations show no failed services, healthy package state, and unchanged listening endpoints apart from expected process-ID changes after restart.
